{"predictors": [
{"name": "Asset Growth Volatility", "construction": "standard deviation of year-over-year changes in total assets over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with more volatile asset growth may be more likely to experience financial distress or management challenges, leading to lower future returns. This volatility can be a proxy for underlying business risk.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Inventory Turnover Acceleration", "construction": "difference between the average inventory turnover ratio over the past 2 years and the average inventory turnover ratio over the past 5 years", "rationale": "An increase in inventory turnover can indicate improving operational efficiency, which may lead to higher future returns. This acceleration can signal a positive shift in a firm's competitive position.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Advertising Expenditure Consistency", "construction": "coefficient of variation of advertising expenditures over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with consistent advertising expenditures may be more likely to have a stable and effective marketing strategy, leading to higher future returns. Inconsistent advertising expenditures can signal underlying business challenges.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "R&D Expense Smoothness", "construction": "standard deviation of year-over-year changes in R&D expenses over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with smoother R&D expense growth may be more likely to have a stable and effective innovation strategy, leading to higher future returns. Volatile R&D expenses can signal underlying management challenges.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Capital Expenditure Momentum", "construction": "year-over-year change in capital expenditures", "rationale": "An increase in capital expenditures can indicate a firm's commitment to investing in its future growth, leading to higher future returns. This momentum can signal a positive shift in a firm's competitive position.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Accounts Payable Days Consistency", "construction": "coefficient of variation of days accounts payable over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with consistent accounts payable days may be more likely to have a stable and effective supply chain management strategy, leading to higher future returns. Inconsistent accounts payable days can signal underlying business challenges.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Tangible Asset Intensity", "construction": "ratio of net property, plant, and equipment to total assets", "rationale": "Firms with higher tangible asset intensity may be more likely to have a stable source of cash flows and lower risk of financial distress, leading to higher future returns. This intensity can be a proxy for underlying business stability.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Pension Fund Asset Allocation", "construction": "percentage of pension fund assets allocated to equity securities", "rationale": "Firms with a higher percentage of pension fund assets allocated to equity securities may be more likely to have a higher expected return on their pension fund investments, leading to higher future returns. This allocation can signal a firm's willingness to take on risk.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Sales Growth Deceleration", "construction": "difference between the average sales growth rate over the past 2 years and the average sales growth rate over the past 5 years", "rationale": "A deceleration in sales growth can indicate a firm's loss of competitive position or market saturation, leading to lower future returns. This deceleration can signal a negative shift in a firm's growth prospects.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
{"name": "Employee Growth Stability", "construction": "coefficient of variation of year-over-year changes in total employees over the past 5 years", "rationale": "Firms with stable employee growth may be more likely to have a well-managed and efficient workforce, leading to higher future returns. Unstable employee growth can signal underlying management challenges or business volatility.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}
]}
